findings.title: Sudoers rule grants root-equivalent access to the `manta` account
findings.description:
The header says "exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider". Three entries are wider than that:

- **`MT_INSTALL` runs a user-owned script as root.** The rule allows `/home/manta/.../deploy/install-production.sh --ref *` as root. That file lives in the operator's own checkout, which `manta` can write. Anyone who can edit the script, or who gets `manta` access, gets unrestricted root. `--ref *` is also unconstrained. To close the hole, the script would have to be root-owned and non-writable by `manta` (for example, installed under `/usr/local/sbin`). The rule would then name that path.
- **Sudoers `*` also matches spaces.** `systemctl stop mt-*` therefore matches `systemctl stop mt-x sshd.service`, and the same applies to `start` and `restart`. The wildcard is not limited to `mt-` units.
- **`MT_RUN` is broad.** `/usr/local/bin/mt-run *` passes any arguments through. As root, `deploy/mt-run` executes the production `mt` CLI with the credentials from `/etc/manta-trading.env`. `MT_READ` also lets `manta` read that file outright. The repository's `cutover_common.py` does use that read (line 226), so it is intentional, but it should be documented as a deliberate exposure of secrets.

The file also names only the 921-related commands. The 265 and 268 cutover scripts issue `sudo tee`, `cp` and `grep` against the env file, and the header's claim does not cover those.

findings.title: `[WAIT]` and `FAIL` verdict markers are scattered string literals
findings.description: `[WAIT]` is defined as a literal in `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py:288`. The cutover script then matches it by substring at lines 204, 265 and 273, next to the existing `"FAIL"` substring checks. The tests repeat it again. Project rules say a comparison value must be defined once. If the producer's wording changes, the cutover silently stops waiting and the `[WAIT]` handling in `ok` stops working. Because `WAIT` is a three-way verdict, a shared constant or an exit code would be sturdier than parsing printed text. Today `run_verify` returns a plain `False` for both FAIL and WAIT, so the caller cannot tell them apart without parsing.

findings.title: The narration log is opened before the working-directory preflight
findings.description: `start_log(NOTES_DIR / ...)` runs before `preflight(args.ref)`. `NOTES_DIR` is a relative path (`cutover_common.py:32`). `preflight` is what checks that the script is running from the dev checkout root (it checks `deploy/` and `.env`, `cutover_common.py:95`). Run from any other directory, the script first creates `project-documents/user/notes/` and a log file there, and only then raises `CutoverError`. Starting the log after `preflight` fixes this. The log also doesn't capture the streamed `run(..., stream=True)` output or the bare `print` lines, only `say`. The docstring calls it "the cutover's report", which overstates what it holds.

findings.title: Cagg freshness compares job finish time with row `created_at`
findings.description: `stale` is `last_successful_finish < max(created_at)`. A refresh materializes the data present when it started, not when it finished. A bar written between the start and finish of the refresh job passes as "fresh" while the cagg has not seen it. The probe also does not account for a refresh policy `end_offset`, which can leave the newest buckets unmaterialized after a successful refresh. The window may be small, but this check exists to prevent a wrong verdict, so the race should at least be documented. Using `last_successful_start`, if the view exposes it, would remove the first problem. I did not verify the `job.hypertable_name = <cagg>` join against a live TimescaleDB, so that join is untested.

findings.title: Import ordering violates the project's ruff `I` rule
findings.description:
The project selects `I` in `pyproject.toml`, but several import blocks look unsorted:

- `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py` lists `NOTES_DIR, fire_unit_until, start_log, CutoverError, fire_unit, …`.
- `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py` puts `cagg_freshness_for_session` before `CheckReport`.
- `minute.py` inserts the `daemon.minute_sessions` and `gaps.compute_missing_ranges` imports ahead of `gaps.minute_coverage`.
- `test_repair_921.py` puts `cagg_freshness_for_session` before `SymbolFindings`.

Run `ruff check --select I --fix` on these files.

findings.title: Test setup is copy-pasted and one test duplicates `_run`
findings.description: `test_last_bar_before_the_chunk_end_is_still_success` re-implements the roughly 50-line mock harness that `_run` already provides, with only different bounds and bars. `TestTruncatedDayAwareSeeding` repeats the connection, transaction and lock mocks a third time. `_run` should accept `bounds` and `gap_end` parameters and the shared mocks should become fixtures in `conftest.py`. The tests also patch about ten internals of `_do_minute_symbol`, so they assert wiring more than behavior. The pure `minute_sessions` tests are good and cover the key predicate.

findings.title: Session judgement may skip a session that opens before the chunk
findings.description: `fetch_session_bounds(conn, symbol, chunk_start, chunk_end)` filters on `session_open_utc >= chunk_start`. A session that opened before `chunk_start` and closes inside the chunk is not judged, so `judge_chunk_by_sessions` finds no judgeable session and keeps the classifier verdict. Chunks are normally session-aligned, so this is probably benign. The new tests do not exercise it. The change also opens an extra pool connection per chunk for what is a small read.

findings.title: Behavioral change in the trailing-weekend tolerance
findings.description: The old four-day tolerance is replaced by session judgement. A response with zero bars in a session now yields PARTIAL and keeps the row. That is the intent, and the PARTIAL path increments `attempt_count`. A session the provider never publishes, such as a calendar-listed day with no data, will eventually reach `RETRY_EXHAUSTED`. That outcome seems acceptable, but it is a new route to `RETRY_EXHAUSTED`.

findings.title: Timer, constants and tests stay consistent
findings.description: `MINUTE_PASS_FIRING_TIMES_UTC`, `mt-minute-pass.timer`, the constants docstrings and the test expectations all move to 04:05 and 07:05. A grep of `.py`, `.timer`, `.service` and `.sh` files found no leftover 01:05 references. `_latest_bar_dt` is removed with no remaining callers. The UTC formatting fix in `check_minute_session_mass` is correct.
